703713.t: In view of the lack of a good etymology, Beekes considers the possibility of a Pre-Greek origin.

703734.t: Univerbation of δι’ (di’), apocopic form of διά (diá, “because of”), and ὅτι (hóti, “that”, conjunction).

703741.t: From earlier δϝίς (dwĭ́s), from Proto-Hellenic *dwís, from Proto-Indo-European *dwís; related to δύο (dŭ́o, “two”). Cognates include the Sanskrit द्विस् (dvís) and the Latin bis and dis-.

703791.t: Perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *dóḱs(e)h₂, from *deḱ- (“to accept”) (whence δοκέω (dokéō)) or with some other influence directly from δοκέω (dokéō).

703775.t: According to Beekes, derived from δέχομαι (dékhomai, “to take, accept”), from Proto-Indo-European *deḱ- (“to take”). Cognate to Latin doceō (“to teach, show, rehearse”) and Latin dignus (“fitting, worthy”).

703702.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *díkā, from Proto-Indo-European *díḱeh₂, from the root *deyḱ- (“to point, show”). Closely related to δείκνυμι (deíknūmĭ, “to show”).

703756.t: From earlier διχθά (dĭkhthắ), from δίς (dĭ́s, “twice”). The velar derivation is unclear; compare Sanskrit द्विधा (dvidhā, “by two”), the dh of which might be found in δι-χ-θά.

703790.t: From Proto-Hellenic *dómos, from Proto-Indo-European *dṓm. Cognates include Latin domus, Sanskrit दम (dáma), Russian дом (dom), and Old Armenian տուն (tun).

703762.t: According to Beekes, probably from Pre-Greek, based on an analysis δίπ-σα (díp-sa) lacking clear semantic and morphological correspondences in other Indo-European branches, as well as the existence of variants with φ and β.

703742.t: Furnée pointed out that the traditional derivation from *δίκ-σκος (*dík-skos), from δικεῖν (dikeîn, “to cast”) is hardly possible, because the suffix “-σκο-” is rare in nominal derivation.

703738.t: From an earlier verbal adjective *δίπλατος (*dĭ́plătos), from Proto-Indo-European *dwi-*pl̥-to-s (“twofold”); compare English twofold. By surface analysis, δι- (dĭ-) + -πλάσιος (-plắsĭos).

703718.t: Etymology tree Ancient Greek διοικέω (dioikéō) Ancient Greek -τις (-tĭs) Ancient Greek -σις (-sĭs) Ancient Greek διοίκησις From διοικέω (dioikéō) + -σις (-sĭs), from δια- (dia-) + οἶκος (oîkos, “house”).

703720.t: From δια- (dĭă-, “across”) + οἰκοδομέω (oikodoméō, “to build a house”).

703714.t: Univerbation of δι’ ὅ (di’ hó); see διά (dĭắ, “because of”) and ὅ (hó, “which”).

703768.t: Beekes claims it is of Pre-Greek origin. Probably from δίω.

703752.t: The origin is uncertain, possibly from Proto-Hellenic *dipʰtʰérā. Related to διψάρα (dipsára, “writing-tablet; piece of leather”) and Mycenaean Greek 𐀇𐁇𐀨 (di-pte-ra).

703701.t: From δικάζω (dĭkắzō, “to judge”) + -της (-tēs, “-er”, masculine agent-noun suffix): Literally, “judger”.

703703.t: Traditionally derived from a u-stem formation of δικεῖν (dikeîn, “to throw”).

703787.t: Traditionally derived from a Proto-Indo-European *delH- (“to reckon”) (which De Vaan considers to be possibly the same root as *delh₁- (“to split”)), and compared with Latin dolus (“fraud, malice”), Oscan dolom (“intention, ruse”), Proto-Germanic *talō…

703797.t: From δέρω (dérō, “to skin, to flay”) + -α (-ā, “nominal suffix”).

703719.t: From διοικέω (dĭoikéō, “to manage, administer”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).
